text:
URE ANSWERS (captured 2026-05-27 via team-lead relay; re-persisting after harness restart killed coordinator before relay). *** SCOPE-CHANGING OVERRIDE — read carefully ***

Q8 [5wbhm status audit — claim statement]: Question presented as trivial-case sign-off (expected verdict 'confirmed'). USER chose OVERRIDE: 'Substantive URE input — reword the claim statement'. Then when asked for exact wording, USER RESPONSE (VERBATIM):

  'Go is the authoritative implementation of the SKILL.md generation pipeline, but has only been verified for 7 skills. Python generation pipeline and content is slightly less up-to-date for these 7 skills, but the rest would be used as reference as they haven't been fully ported over yet.'

IMPACT — this is NO LONGER a trivial 'confirmed' status audit. The reworded claim has TWO parts that change the audit shape:
1. Authority is QUALIFIED, not absolute: Go authoritative but verified for only 7 skills => expected verdict shifts from 'confirmed' toward 'qualified'.
2. Coverage overlay: the deliverable must ENUMERATE which 7 skills are Go-verified vs the remaining (~30) that still use Python pipeline/content as reference because they aren't fully ported.

REVISED 5wbhm scope for PROPOSAL drafting:
- Claim (verbatim above) replaces the pre-filled 'Go authoritative; Python deprecated' claim.
- Verdict vocabulary unchanged: confirmed/refuted/qualified — but expected verdict is now 'qualified'.
- Evidence must establish: (a) WHICH 7 skills are verified Go-authoritative, (b) that Python is 'slightly less up-to-date' for those 7 (i.e., Go is ahead), (c) that the other skills still rely on Python as reference (not yet ported).
- Deliverable (pasture/AGENTS.md 'Code generation' section) must include the 7-skill enumeration + the not-yet-ported remainder, not just a binary authority statement.
- Cross-reference x5071 (port remaining 30 Python skills) — the 'not fully ported' remainder is exactly x5071's scope.

Note: this couples 5wbhm to the 7-overlapping-skills set referenced in PYTHON_TO_GO_MIGRATION.md + ROADMAP §1i (skill-drift CI check across 7 overlapping skills). Coordinator should reconcile 'the 7' against that doc when drafting.

text:
mh4ek coverage audit complete. Deliverable: docs/audits/mh4ek-constraint-coverage.md

ESCALATION per PROPOSAL-1 §10 — two non-trivial semantic judgment calls requiring team-lead review before UAT:

1. C-review-binary (verdict: divergent): Python enforces via string-level check; Go enforces via VoteType typed enum (compile-time structural prevention). Same constraint intent, different mechanism. Request team-lead judgment: is 'type system prevents invalid values at compile time' equivalent to the Python runtime check, or is it a semantic gap?

C-worker-gates (verdict: divergent): Spans two Python methods. check_blocker_gate() (blocker count check) IS ported and tested in Go. check_worker_gates() (has_todos + tests_pass + typecheck_pass quality gates) is entirely absent from Go runtime. - True constraint count: 27 (constraints.py SoT) + 1 addendum (C-actionable-errors, catalog-only)
- Verdicts: 1 ported (C-review-consensus), 0 untested, 24 missing, 2 divergent (C-worker-gates, C-review-binary)
- 28 gap tasks filed (all discovered-from:aura-plugins-mh4ek, aura:residual, P3)
- Key surprise: Go has NO RuntimeConstraintChecker equivalent — ActivityCheckConstraints only implements consensus+blocker gates via state machine; all other C-* IDs exist only as codegen schema metadata

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE 11 UAT (mh4ek) cont. 2026-05-30 — BUCKET A answer + MAJOR ARCHITECTURAL FINDING surfaced by user.

BUCKET A QUESTION presented: 'These 3 (C-review-consensus/C-review-binary/C-actionable-errors) are machine-enforced in Go at level (1)programmatic-check-or-(2)type-system, not (3)prompt-only. Disposition?'
USER RESPONSE (verbatim): 'Accept all 3 as enforced — close their verify-tasks (Recommended)'.

USER RESPONSE 2 (verbatim, architectural challenge): 'I'm confused here: does the type-system guarantee have to do with the multi-agent orchestrator pastured or pasture-msg, or does it have to do with the skill generation or schema generation? Because the orchestrator does NOT have to be used or mentioned by the corresponding skills.'

COORDINATOR VERIFIED (grep, 2026-05-30) — USER IS CORRECT. The pasture Go codebase has TWO DISJOINT halves:
(1) ORCHESTRATOR: pastured (Temporal worker) + pasture-msg (control CLI) + internal/temporal. Real (1)/(2) enforcement lives ONLY here: consensus gate (ValidateAdvance), blocker gate, VoteType enum (votes via 'pasture-msg signal vote' → RecordVote).
(2) SKILL+BD layer: internal/codegen generates skills/*/SKILL.md; agents execute via bd. Reviewer SKILL.md L278 votes via FREE-TEXT 'bd comments add <id> "VOTE: ACCEPT - ..."'. Supervisor SKILL.md uses only bd. NO skill references pasture-msg/pastured/temporal (only install-cli does).

NO BRIDGE: nothing reads bd 'VOTE:' comments → RecordVote signal. workflow_review.go does not read bd tasks. The two halves never touch. The SAME codegen that owns VoteType emits the instruction to bypass it (specs_data_body.go:1876).

IMPLICATION (reframes mh4ek verdict): In the execution model agents ACTUALLY use (skill+bd), even C-review-consensus and C-review-binary are (3) prompt-only — their (1)/(2) enforcement exists only in the orchestrator, which the agent workflow never invokes. Only C-actionable-errors genuinely binds at runtime — and only for the pasture TOOLS' OWN error output (internal/* packages), not protocol artifacts.

=> Bucket A revised: C-actionable-errors = confirmed-enforced (scope: tool errors). C-review-binary + C-review-consensus = enforced-ONLY-IF-orchestrated; (3) prompt-only in the skill+bd path. The gap-vs-design verdict for the whole audit now hinges on: IS the Temporal orchestrator intended to be in the loop, or is skill+bd the primary model? Surfacing to user as the pivotal question.

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE 11 UAT (mh4ek) — PIVOTAL ARCHITECTURE DECISION (user, 2026-05-30).

QUESTION presented: 'Orchestrator (pastured/pasture-msg) has real (1)/(2) enforcement but skills never invoke it + no bd<->Temporal bridge. What is the INTENDED relationship between orchestrator and skill+bd agent workflow?' Options: orchestrator-primary-not-wired / skill+bd-primary-orchestrator-optional / bridge-the-two / defer-to-vji97.

USER RESPONSE (verbatim): 'Skill+bd is the primary model; orchestrator is optional/future observability' + elaboration: 'The current skills / agents / schema are the prioritized, near-term driver. Once we have all of the generators for these ported to Golang, the multi-agent orchestrator should be the primary driver, integrated with running agents via skills + hooks.'

=> PHASED ARCHITECTURE (binding decision rule for mh4ek verdict):
- NEAR-TERM (now): skill+bd is primary. Enforcement layers that COUNT now = (a) generated SKILL.md guidance (3), (b) pasture-task CLI validation, (c) Claude Code hooks. Priority = finish porting the generators (skill-gen, schema-gen) to Go.
- FUTURE (after all generators ported to Go): Temporal orchestrator becomes primary driver, integrated with agents via skills + hooks. The orchestrator's (1)/(2) gates (consensus, blocker, VoteType) activate THEN.

DECISION RULE for each constraint's disposition:
- Enforced by type/convention regardless of orchestrator (e.g. C-actionable-errors via StructuredError on tool errors) => confirmed-enforced.
- Workflow-state gates living in orchestrator (consensus, blocker, clean-review-exit, max-cycles, worker-quality-gates) => by-design: near-term SKILL.md guidance, FUTURE orchestrator enforcement. Not a near-term gap.
- Agent-judgment constraints (explore-ephemeral, vertical-slices, ure-verbatim, integration-points, followup-*, severity-*, etc.) => by-design: SKILL.md guidance is the intended near-term layer.
- Mechanically checkable in CLI (dep-direction, naming regex, leaf>=1, slice-review-before-close, never-delete) or hook (agent-commit, supervisor-no-impl) => CANDIDATE near-term enforcement upgrades; user decides per-item whether to machine-back now vs leave as guidance.

mh4ek verdict moves PROVISIONAL -> RESOLVED-QUALIFIED: audit documents the two-worlds architecture + per-constraint near-term enforcement layer. Continuing per-item walk for the CLI/hook candidates.

text:
PLAN-REVIEW B (round 2) — TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY — VOTE: ACCEPT

ROUND-1 RESOLUTION:
- B-B1 (D4 delete) RESOLVED: change #2 + D4' remove the delete; sup-review-severity-groups/impl-rev-b3 PROMOTED to frag-rev-severity-groups. Verified the delete would have dangled 'Per [...]' refs at specs_data_body.go:605 (supervisor) and :1986 (impl-review) and stripped the directive from supervisor+impl-review (C-severity-eager renders only into reviewer via roleConstraints).
- B-I1 (owner-key namespace) RESOLVED: owners derived; keys in SkillBodySpecs dir-key space (map keyed by dir-string @specs_data_body.go:12; render lookups @skills.go:447 string(roleID) + :493 subSkillDirKey).

NEW IMPORTANT (1): Existing passing test TestSkillBodySpecsCompleteness (specs_test.go:332) iterates SkillBodySpecs[key].Sections/.Behaviors and asserts non-empty Title/Content (lines 405/410) + non-empty behavior ID/Given/When/Then/ShouldNot (lines 426-435). Proposal says 'mirrored Go tests' but does not call out updating THIS existing test to skip FragmentID-only marker entries. Mechanical fix, but must be in SLICE-3/4 scope. (Note: ValidateSkillStructure @markdown.go:54 operates on RENDERED markdown post-resolution, so it does NOT choke on markers — only this struct-level test does.)

Already surfaced for UAT (D1); flagging for the record.

SINGLE-SOURCE FEASIBILITY: OK.
- Markers coexist+resolve: []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec are plain ordered slices; pre-render pass at skills.go:447/:493 swaps markers for resolved fragments before ctx assignment — placement preserved (slice order), deterministic.
- FragmentToOwnerRefs(): direct analog of working ConstraintToRoleRefs() (context.go:577) inverting a consumer-keyed map. Feasible.
- Checks runnable at tools/codegen/main.go: already collects errors + os.Exit(1); add ValidateGlobalIDs() before the loop to fail go generate. Feasible.

EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED: severity-tree prose is BYTE-IDENTICAL (len=1525) after canonicalizing the Per[] ref; all 6 review-behavior pairs (sup-review-* <-> impl-rev-b1..b6) are byte-identical in G/W/T/ShouldNot (only IDs differ).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
PHASE-4 PLAN REVIEW ROUND 2 — Reviewer C (ELEGANCE / complexity-matching lens). Independent Opus re-review of PROPOSAL-2 (revises PROPOSAL-1 after 3/3 REVISE). Verified against code: context.go (roleConstraints/ConstraintToRoleRefs), specs.go (SkillBody/ProseSection/BehaviorSpec), skills.go:447-451/495-497 (body→ctx copy), templates/skill.go.tmpl:198-217 (range BodyBehaviors/BodySections), specs_data_body.go (dup clusters + Per[...] cross-refs).

VOTE: ACCEPT

ROUND-1 RESOLUTION (C-I1/C-I2/C-I3/C-M1/C-M2):
- C-I1 (owners-on-fragment INVERTS pattern): RESOLVED. Change#1+D1 drop `Owners`. Single source = consumer placement markers (consumer-keyed, exactly like roleConstraints[role]={cid}); FragmentToOwnerRefs() is the DERIVED inversion, mirroring ConstraintToRoleRefs() verbatim. Faithful single-source mirror. No residual dual-source.
- C-I2 (dual-source + reconciliation): RESOLVED. §5 states "NO reconciliation check (ownership definitional)"; D1 "Removes dual-source + the reconciliation check." Clean.
- C-I3 (D4 conflates rendering surfaces — the BLOCKER): RESOLVED. Change#2 → D4' promote-not-delete. Verified: C-severity-eager lives ONLY in roleConstraints[RoleReviewer] (context.go:151; supervisor count=0), so deleting sup-review-severity-groups/impl-rev-b3 would strip the directive from supervisor+impl-review (they never receive it via the constraint) AND dangle Per[...] prose at specs_data_body.go:605/:1986. Promote-and-share is correct.
- C-M1 (one-payload validated not commented): RESOLVED. §1 "exactly one payload per Kind (VALIDATED, not commented)" + §5(c) in ValidateGlobalIDs.
- C-M2 (frag-{domain}-* naming): RESOLVED. Change#6 + migration table use frag-rev-* throughout.

NEW BLOCKER: none.
NEW IMPORTANT: none.

MINOR (non-blocking):
- M1: Change#3 cross-ref canonicalization rewrites prose 'Per [sup-review-severity-groups]'/'Per [impl-rev-b3]' to the canonical frag id. Since the behavior template renders **[{{.ID}}]** literally (skill.go.tmpl:200), the canonical id (e.g. frag-rev-severity-groups) becomes the VISIBLE marker text in every consumer — D7 acknowledges this. The user-facing prose will read "Per [frag-rev-severity-groups]" — slightly less mnemonic than the old role-scoped id, but it IS the only way to make shared prose strictly-identical (R3) and is correct. Worth a golden-diff eyeball at UAT that the rendered phrasing reads naturally.
- M2: SLICE-5 (R7) leaves "in-epoch vs follow-on" to UAT. Fine, but the slice's only deliverable (extend ValidateGlobalIDs to agent/role-behavior/handoff namespace) overlaps SLICE-2's validator. If kept in-epoch, fold into SLICE-2 to avoid a near-empty slice; if deferred, drop SLICE-5 from this plan. Either is clean — flag for UAT.

MARKER-MECHANISM ELEGANCE (struct-overload vs distinct FragmentRef):
The marker is a ProseSection/BehaviorSpec with only FragmentID set, acting as an in-slice placeholder. This IS a mild type-overload (the struct is both content-carrier and ref). A distinct tiny `FragmentRef{ID string}` type would be more self-documenting and would let the validator distinguish "ref" from "malformed empty section" structurally rather than by zero-value sniffing. HOWEVER the overload is JUSTIFIED here: (a) SkillBody.Sections/Behaviors are typed []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec — a FragmentRef would force a third slice or an interface, complicating SkillBody and the templates; (b) D5's whole value is templates-unchanged + pre-render resolution; a separate ref type breaks that by adding a new field/branch. The overload keeps the marker at the exact slice position with zero template churn, and ValidateGlobalIDs §5(b) already enforces "every FragmentID marker resolves," so the zero-value-sniff is checked, not silent. RECOMMENDATION: keep the overload as proposed; it matches the existing []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec grain and is the lower-complexity choice. Optionally (MINOR) add a helper constructor (e.g. fragRef(id) / behaviorRef(id)) in the registry so call sites read as refs, not half-empty structs — pure readability, no type change.

COMPLEXITY-MATCH vs URD: Proportionate. Registry mirrors ConstraintSpecs (R2/R4); strictly-identical via distinct fragments not parameterization (R3 — no override knobs); build-time hard error mirrors existing validator grain (R5); promote-not-delete preserves the 29-skill no-regression priority (P1). No over-reach (no plugin system, no per-consumer variation). No under-reach (one-payload + resolve + uniqueness all build-failed, not test-only). R7 appropriately minimal post-rescope (audit found agents source RoleSpec.Behaviors / handoffs are field-driven → no shareable body-prose there today, so SLICE-5 is just namespace-uniformity, not a second mechanism). Slice breakdown (mechanism → validator → behavior-migrate+canonicalize → vote-options/blocker-dual-parent reconcile → R7 namespace) is a clean dependency order.

NEW INCONSISTENCY from the revision: none found. The revision is internally consistent; the canonical picks + one-payload validation + derived owners all align with the roleConstraints precedent.

SUMMARY: PROPOSAL-2 correctly adopts the round-1 simplification (drop Owners; derive owners from consumer placement markers as the inverse of consumer-keyed inclusion), faithfully mirroring ConstraintSpec/roleConstraints/ConstraintToRoleRefs. The D4 BLOCKER is resolved by promote-not-delete with verified rationale (C-severity-eager is reviewer-only). One-payload is validated; naming adopted; no dual-source residue. The marker struct-overload is the justified low-complexity choice given the existing []ProseSection/[]BehaviorSpec template grain. Zero BLOCKER, zero IMPORTANT → ACCEPT. Two MINOR (canonical-id prose readability eyeball at UAT; SLICE-5 fold-or-defer) are non-blocking.

Over/under-engineering: parity enforcement is proportionate (build-fail + test = the user's explicit 'YES' decision; makes 'one source of truth' a compile guarantee, not belt-and-suspenders). Nothing speculative beyond typed-refs + parity.

Note (doc accuracy, not a code issue): description says it mirrors 'RoleId/PhaseId/CommandId' — there is NO CommandId type in the codebase (CommandSpec.Id is bare string, comment-only 'CommandId wire value' at specs.go:153). author: David Huu Pham
text:
## URE — Verbatim Q&A record (3 rounds, AskUserQuestion)

### Round 1

#### Q1 [I7 clean exit]
Q: "I7 (clean-review exit) vs the existing 3-cycle cap. Today the protocol caps review-fix cycles at 3 per slice, and PROCESS.md allows exiting after cycle 3 'with IMPORTANT findings remaining → FOLLOWUP; proceed' — meaning the very last fixes might never get re-reviewed. Your feedback says a wave MUST end on a clean re-review round. How should these reconcile?"
Options presented:
  - "Re-review is exempt from cap": 3-cycle cap counts only fix-generating rounds; a final fix-free re-review always required, doesn't count to cap; BLOCKERs block, IMPORTANTs may still defer after clean re-review.
  - "Hard clean or escalate": MUST end 0 BLOCKER+0 IMPORTANT via fresh reviewers; if cycle 3 dirty, escalate to architect; remove proceed-dirty.
  - "Keep cap, add re-review gate only": leave 3-cycle+FOLLOWUP as-is, just require fixes re-reviewed once before close.
A (verbatim, custom): "Remove cap for now, unlimited cycles"

#### Q2 [I6 fix workflow]
Q: "I6 (fix-request validation cases). How heavyweight should fix-type handling be — eliciting validation cases in the URE, confirming them in the UAT, and turning failing real-data cases into fixtures during implementation?"
Options: "Full lifecycle + new axis" (request-type axis fix|feature|chore|refactor; URE elicits validation cases, UAT confirms, workers evaluate+fixture failing cases; new C-fix-validation-cases + shared fragment) / "Lightweight, no new axis" / "Elicit + confirm only".
A (verbatim): "Full lifecycle"

#### Q3 [I10 scope]
Q: "I10 (SendMessage tool grant). Which generated agent definitions should receive the SendMessage tool in their frontmatter?"
Options: "All 5 roles" (epoch, architect, supervisor, worker, reviewer) / "Supervisor + worker + epoch" / "Supervisor + worker only".
A (verbatim): "All 5 roles"

#### Q4 [I3 strength]
Q: "I3 (interface-first decomposition) — strength of the rule. Combined with I9 (slices may have any number of leaf tasks)."
Options: "Soft preference" / "Strong SHOULD + rationale" (architect SHOULD default to interface-first slice, must justify linear in IMPL_PLAN) / "Hard rule".
A (verbatim): "Strong SHOULD + rationale"

### Round 2

#### Q5 [I7 clean def]
Q: "Since I7 removes the cycle cap (iterate until clean), what exactly defines 'clean' for closing a review wave? Today 'clean' = 0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT, with MINOR allowed to defer to a FOLLOWUP epic."
Options: "0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT" (IMPORTANTs must be fixed, only MINOR defers; iterate until holds) / "0 BLOCKER only" (IMPORTANTs may defer after re-review).
A (verbatim): "0 BLOCKER + 0 IMPORTANT"

#### Q6 [I7 safety valve]
Q: "With no hard cap, how do we guard against an infinite review-fix loop without re-introducing 'proceed dirty'?"
Options: "Advisory escalation, never auto-proceed" / "Pure unlimited" (no valve, iterate until clean, rely on human interruption) / "Escalate to architect re-plan after K".
A (verbatim): "Pure unlimited"

author: David Huu Pham
text:
USER DIRECTIVE (verbatim): "We should also include the syncing of the marketplace with the ./bin/pasture-release sync-versions as well"

Decision: extend `pasture-release registry sync-versions` so it ALSO reconciles each registered plugin's cross-repo marketplace entry — not just intra-plugin file drift (which is all it does today via DiscoverVersionFiles).

Proposed behavior:
- For each registered plugin: read its canonical version (plugin.json = SoT), then look up its registered marketplace entry (FindPlugin already returns the MarketplaceEntry) and compare the entry's version.
- If drifted, report a VersionDrift and (unless --dry-run) write the corrected version into the marketplace's plugins[<name>].version, leaving the marketplace's own metadata.version untouched (same rule as the --plugin step-9 sync).
- Keep file-write-only semantics (no auto commit/push); existing --dry-run flag applies.
- This would have caught the v0.0.1→0.0.2 drift this task came from (sync-versions said "version-consistent" because it ignored the marketplace entry).

Immediate manual fix already applied: marketplace pasture entry bumped 0.0.1→0.0.2 on main (aura-plugins 3c78b46); parent submodule re-pointed to released pasture main 5589bc7 (v0.0.2).

author: David Huu Pham
text:
IMPL-UAT verification (team-lead, real binary) — FOUND PRE-EXISTING BUG in non-TTY detection (guard identical since 81b6959; C1/C2 commit 7a675d0 did not introduce it):
stdinIsTTY uses `info.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice` to mean 'is a terminal'. But /dev/null is ALSO a character device -> misdetected as a TTY. Observed (at 7a675d0):
  - `sync-versions </dev/null` (classic CI non-interactive) -> PROMPTS + 'Aborted' + exit 0  [WRONG; ratified C3 says error+exit1]
  - `printf 'n\n' | sync-versions` (pipe) -> errors 'refusing... non-TTY' + exit 1  [errors, but inconsistent]
Real TTY: only an actual terminal should prompt. Fix = proper isatty (golang.org/x/term IsTerminal(fd), already transitively in go.sum; or x/sys/unix IoctlGetTermios but that needs windows build-tags). Tests passed because they STUB stdinIsTTY — the DEFAULT impl is what's wrong; add a test of the real default against /dev/null + pipe + (best-effort) tty.
SAFETY: still safe (never applies unconfirmed writes); deviation is exit-code/UX (/dev/null aborts exit0 instead of error exit1). Pending user decision on dep + scope.

User confirmed (2026-06-06): DBOS supports a Go SDK AND a SQLite backend — resolves the earlier open question; DBOS (embedded durable execution, no separate server, Go+SQLite) is the leading candidate vs option 3 (plain state-machine-over-SQLite). No existing GitHub issue for orchestrator-engine buildout or provenance integration (provenance integ tracked only in bd aura-plugins-9wdwc + ROADMAP §2q). author: David Huu Pham
text: Phase-1 research done: DBOS-Go + pure-Go SQLite (SqliteSystemDB w/ modernc) CONFIRMED first-class single-machine, CGO-free, crash-recoverable. Ranking: 1) DBOS-Go+SQLite 2) plain-SQLite-state-machine 3) keep-Temporal. DBOS pre-1.0 (v0.16.0) → pin + kill-9 resume spike before commit. Full report on pasture#13. PROPOSAL-1 REVISE-1 (addresses plan-review-B REVISE; A correctness + C elegance already ACCEPT).

## Test-plan additions to SLICE-1 L4 (resolve B's two gaps)
(a) INJECTABLE git-metadata gatherer: HookRecord takes a gatherer dependency (func(sha string) (map[string]string, error), default = real-git gatherGitMeta). Unit test injects a FAKE gatherer to verify merge precedence WITHOUT shelling git: explicit --message/--author/--branch/--timestamp flags OVERRIDE git-derived values; git-derived fills only when the flag is absent.
(b) REAL-GIT integration test: git init a t.TempDir() repo + make a commit; run HookRecord with --sha ONLY (no metadata flags); assert the git-derived message/author/branch/timestamp landed in the recorded row. (c) PAYLOAD-DECODE verification: add a test helper (or inline) that SELECTs audit_events.payload and JSON-decodes it, asserting sha + each metadata key/value is present. The existing queryAuditEvent helper does NOT select the payload column, so 'metadata in payload' was previously unverifiable — this makes the assertion performable.

- Exit codes: reuse errors.ExitCode(err); the handler must errors.As-unwrap the *dispatchErrors aggregate (hooks.go) to reach the underlying *StructuredError Category (the top-level Dispatch error is not itself structured). Do NOT hand-roll a 0/1/5 switch.

VOTE: ACCEPT (Reviewer B / TEST QUALITY, round 1) — SLICE-1 epoch-6l5yo

AXIS=TestQuality BLOCKER=0 IMPORTANT=0 MINOR=3

All three REVISE-1 mandatory test-plan additions are present and the assertions are REAL (not stubs); tests compile and pass (handlers 42s, hooks 2.3s, cmd/pasture 53s, all ok). Coverage: HookRecord 87.5%, mergeMeta 100%, gatherGitMeta 100%, parse/list 100%.

REVISE-1 verification:
(a) Injectable gatherer, BOTH directions: TestHookRecord_MergePrecedence_FlagsOverrideGit (flags win where set, git fills where absent) + _GitFillsWhenFlagsAbsent (no flags → all git). Fake gatherer injected; no git shelled. Real assertions via payload decode. ✓
(b) Real-git integration: TestHookRecord_RealGit_DerivesMetadataFromCommit — git init temp repo (-b trunk) + deterministic identity + real commit, HookRecord with --sha ONLY (Gatherer nil → production gatherGitMeta via t.Chdir), asserts message/author/branch=trunk/timestamp landed. (c) Payload-decode: decodeAuditPayload SELECTs audit_events.payload, JSON-decodes, asserts sha + each metadata key/value via assertString (real value equality, not non-nil). 'metadata in payload' genuinely verified. ✓
(d) Error cases: TestHookRecord_UnknownEvent_ActionableError (asserts CategoryValidation + exit 1 + Fix lists 'git-commit') and _MissingSHA_ActionableError (whitespace-only → validation + exit 1). Actionable content asserted, not just 'an error'. ✓
Integration smoke: TestHookRecord_WritesOneGitCommitRowAndEdge — temp pasture.db dispatch asserts exactly ONE GitCommit row (event_type filter), sha in payload, exactly one ContextGit edge keyed on sha. ✓
6 git_recorder_test.go updates: STRENGTHENED not weakened — TestGitRecorder_DispatchesViaManager now asserts countAuditEventsByType(EventGitCommit)==1 (the actual row) in addition to the edge; fixture + 4 Handle tests + RegisterDefaultRecorders now dispatch HookGitCommit, mirroring production wiring. The dispatch→record path is meaningfully exercised via the new event. ✓
Principles: SUT (HookRecord + full Manager wire + real SQLite) NOT mocked; only the git gatherer dependency is faked. Observable outcomes asserted (DB rows, exit codes, error category/content). Shared fixtures (strptr, decodeAuditPayload, countContextEdges, requireValidationError). No flaky time/sleep/ordering in the new hook tests. Cobra-wiring test absence is the explicitly-DEFERRED REVISE-1 item and matches the project's handler-level convention (no cmd/* test invokes RunE). storage-exit-5 must-fail also explicitly deferred. ✓

MINOR findings (do NOT block; all severities must still reach 0 before wave close):
- MINOR-1 (hook_test.go / hook.go:198-206): the documented 'explicit empty-flag override' semantic (flag != nil but *flag=="" wins over a git-derived value) is never asserted as an observable outcome. mergeMeta shows 100% line coverage but no test distinguishes strptr("")+git-has-value → payload value is "" (override) vs git value (fill). Fix: add a case to TestHookRecord_MergePrecedence_FlagsOverrideGit with Message: strptr("") while the fake gatherer returns a non-empty message, asserting payload[message]=="". Cheap, pins the type-doc contract.
- MINOR-2 (hook_test.go:299-317): TestHookRecord_UnknownEvent uses 'if stderrors.As(err,&se)' to guard the Fix-content assertion, so if As() ever fails the supported-events check is silently skipped (the prior requireValidationError already As-asserts, but here the guard could mask a regression). - MINOR-3 (hook_test.go:233 / cmd/pasture/hook.go RunE): the cmd-layer pointer-conversion logic (Changed() → &v for the 4 optional flags, Args: cobra.NoArgs) is untested. author: David Huu Pham
text:
REVIEWER C (ELEGANCE & COMPLEXITY-MATCHING) — SLICE-1 round 1

AXIS=Elegance BLOCKER=0 IMPORTANT=0 MINOR=3
Gates: gofmt clean, go vet clean, go test -race PASS (handlers 47.5s, hooks 3.5s).

VOTE: ACCEPT (no BLOCKER/IMPORTANT; 3 MINOR polish items, non-blocking).

== BLOCKER (0) ==
None. The implementation builds EXACTLY to the ratified design (PROPOSAL-1 + REVISE-1 + plan-UAT): Manager-path seam, HookGitCommit enum, WithSubscribedEvents REPLACING the HookSliceCompleted default, errors.ExitCode-derived exit codes (no hand-rolled 0/1/5 switch), injectable GitMetaGatherer with flag-over-git precedence, *string absent-vs-empty flags. No design defect breaks the contract.

== IMPORTANT (0) ==
None.
- Cobra RunE -> standalone handler convention is a near-exact copy of cmd/pasture/migrate.go (code, hErr := handlers.X(); printError(hErr); exitWithCode(code); return nil). Perfect match.
- Handler-does-validation (not cobra MarkFlagRequired) matches task_events.go and is justified: keeps validation testable at handler level + yields actionable StructuredErrors. Consistent.
- *string optional flags to distinguish absent (git may fill) vs explicit-empty (override) is idiomatic and well-documented; mergeMeta encodes the precedence cleanly.
- gatherGitMeta is cleanly isolated behind the GitMetaGatherer func-type seam (injectable, best-effort, never errors). Not leaky.
- Typed SupportedHookEvent enum + hookEventBindings map is the right shape for the ratified extensible seam — minimal, statically defined, no speculative plugin machinery. Complexity proportional to the problem.
- Pre-existing lint items (dispatchErrors.Error() string-builder in hooks.go; no query_test.go exists in internal/hooks) confirmed genuinely pre-existing / untouched by this diff and correctly left out-of-scope.

== MINOR (3) ==

MINOR-C1: Stringly-typed 'sha' key duplicated in handler.
  internal/handlers/hook.go:172 — data := map[string]any{"sha": sha}.
  The hooks package already EXPORTS the canonical key as a typed constant: hooks.GitCommitDataKey = "sha" (git_recorder.go:59), and the recorder uses it everywhere (Handle reads data[GitCommitDataKey]). The handler — the producer that must agree with that consumer — hardcodes the bare string instead. This is exactly the cross-package key-drift the typed-constant convention exists to prevent.
  FIX: data := map[string]any{hooks.GitCommitDataKey: sha}.

MINOR-C2: Two-source supported-event set (slice + map keys must stay in sync).
  internal/handlers/hook.go:64-73 — supportedHookEvents []SupportedHookEvent AND hookEventBindings map[SupportedHookEvent]hooks.HookEvent both enumerate the same CLI events. The slice exists only to render an ORDERED list in errors/help; the map is the lookup. A future event must be added to BOTH (the comments say so), a two-place edit that can drift. Acceptable for one entry, but the cleaner shape is a single ordered source: derive the list from an ordered []struct{cli; hook} (or keep the map for lookup but generate the display list from a single ordered slice of pairs). Not blocking at N=1.
  FIX (optional): collapse to one ordered source of (cliEvent, hookEvent) pairs; build both the lookup and the display list from it.

MINOR-C3: cliEvent return from parseSupportedHookEvent is near-redundant.
  internal/handlers/hook.go:119,191 — parseSupportedHookEvent returns (cliEvent, hookEvent, err) but cliEvent is only used for the success Fprintf 'recorded %s event for sha %s'. Since parse trims/normalises raw into cliEvent, this is fine, but the 3-value return is slightly heavier than needed; the success message could equally print in.Event (already validated) or a single returned value. Trivial; flag only for tightness.

Naming/placement/DRY otherwise clean: file placement matches (cmd/pasture/hook.go + internal/handlers/hook.go), doc comments are substantive without boilerplate, error messages satisfy what/why/where/impact/fix and read in plain English per errors.go convention, tests assert observable DB outcomes (payload JSON decode + context_edges) not internal state, SUT not mocked (only the git gatherer injected), shared helpers (decodeAuditPayload/countContextEdges) factored. Complexity is proportional. No dead code.

Spec conformance verified:
- MANAGER PATH seam confirmed: HookRecord builds hooks.NewManager()+RegisterDefaultRecorders -> Dispatch(HookPayload{HookGitCommit}) -> GitRecorder.Handle -> RecordCommit -> tasks.RecordGitEvent. NO direct tasks.RecordGitEvent call from the handler. Matches RATIFIED design.
- Subscription = HookGitCommit ONLY via WithSubscribedEvents (replaces default). No recording regression: the old default (HookSliceCompleted) only ever received SHA-less slice payloads which Handle no-ops on, so the swap stops a guaranteed-no-op dispatch, nothing real. 6 sanctioned test updates all consistent; temporal pkg still green.
- Exit codes correct: dispatchErrors.Unwrap() []error + errors.As reaches the underlying *StructuredError; RecordGitEvent returns CategoryStorage (->5) for write failures and CategoryValidation (->1) for bad input; Handle wraps with %w preserving the chain. Storage failure cannot mis-map to 1.
- Metadata merge precedence correct: mergeMeta — non-nil flag wins (incl explicit empty), nil flag -> git fills if present&non-empty. *string distinguishes absent vs empty. No inversion, no nil-deref (default gatherer never returns nil map; flag-only path also safe).
- Actionable errors present for unknown --event (lists supported events incl git-commit) and missing --sha (what/why/where/impact/fix).
- No Temporal coupling introduced (handlers/hooks import only errors/hooks/tasks).
- Resource cleanup: defer tracker.Close()/auditDB.Close() registered immediately post-open; cover all later error + dispatch paths.

MINOR-1 internal/hooks/git_recorder.go:28,75,102,139,254ff doc comments — Stale post-graduation prose. Package doc + NewGitRecorder still say the default sub is HookSliceCompleted and "until [HookGitCommit] lands, callers stick with the default"; that future has arrived (RegisterDefaultRecorders now always overrides to HookGitCommit). Why it matters: misleading to the next maintainer about the production wiring. Fix: update the comments to state HookGitCommit is the production subscription and HookSliceCompleted is a vestigial constructor default only.

MINOR-2 internal/handlers/hook.go:248-279 gatherGitMeta — resolves against process CWD, not the sha's repo. `git show -s <sha>` and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` run in os.Getwd(); running from outside the commit's repo silently yields wrong/empty metadata (best-effort, no error — by contract). Fix: add a doc note that metadata derivation requires running inside the commit's checkout, or accept an optional repo-dir.

MINOR-3 internal/handlers/hook.go:270-275 branch derivation — records the CURRENT HEAD branch (rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD), not the branch commit <sha> belongs to. Coincide for a just-fired post-commit hook; latent gap when recording an older/foreign sha. Fix: document the "current HEAD" semantics in the helper comment.

Severity groups: IMPORTANT + MINOR(non-blocking) noted here; no BLOCKER so slice not blocked by this review on correctness axis.
